result.title: Preface
result.summary: The Apple Valley Fire Protection District is soliciting proposals from qualified consultants for actuarial services to value other post-employment benefits (OPEB) in compliance with GASB Statement No. 75. Respondents should review the RFP’s specifications, terms, and conditions. Proposals are due by 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2024. Submit a PDF by email to Amber Exley at aexley@avfpd.org with the subject “Other Post-Employment Benefits Actuarial Services,” or mail it to Amber Exley, Finance Officer, Apple Valley Fire Protection District, 22400 Headquarters Drive, Apple Valley, CA 92307.

result.title: GENERAL INFORMATION
result.summary: The Apple Valley Fire Protection District (AVFPD) seeks proposals from qualified actuarial firms to value Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) under GASB Statement No. 75 for its financial report as of June 30, 2024, and beyond. Valuations must follow Actuarial Standards Board practices and assumptions and methods prescribed by the CalPERS Board; services and conditions are detailed in the Scope of Work. AVFPD will not reimburse proposal-preparation expenses and may request information or clarification or permit corrections. It may retain all proposals and use ideas from any proposal, whether selected or not. Submitting a proposal signifies acceptance of the request’s conditions unless exceptions are clearly specified and confirmed in the resulting contract. Proposals must be received by 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2024; further submission instructions are in the document.

result.title: BACKGROUND
result.summary: The Apple Valley Fire Protection District (AVFPD), formed in 1951 and incorporated in 1962 under California’s Local Fire District Law, is about 90 miles northeast of Los Angeles. It serves approximately 94,000 residents across 206 square miles, employs 59 full-time staff, and adopted a $15.5 million budget for fiscal year 2024. AVFPD contracts with CalPERS for retirement benefits under Government Code section 22825.5 and reimburses eligible retirees monthly for health insurance, up to a Board-set maximum based on service years and position. The plan closed to new employees on December 1, 2007, except for specified leadership, fire-service, fleet, and administrative positions.

result.title: SCOPE OF WORK
result.summary: AVFPD seeks an actuary to value its OPEB and meet current and future GASB requirements, including Statements 74 and 75. Services include full valuations as of June 30, 2024, 2026, and 2028; roll-forward updates as of June 30, 2025, 2027, and 2029; and recommended contributions and funding for FY 2025–2030. The actuary must provide information for AVFPD’s Comprehensive Annual Financial Report and CalPERS/CERBT submissions, including required certifications, an Excel valuation spreadsheet, and a certified final results outline. The actuary will meet with AVFPD as needed, address auditor and reporting inquiries, support implementation of new pronouncements, and provide ongoing consultation. Working papers and reports must be retained at the actuary’s expense for at least seven years after the contract’s final year, made available to AVFPD and successors, and support audits and reporting. AVFPD may publish reports unless use could mislead or a material subsequent event affects them. Proposals must state annual all-inclusive, not-to-exceed fees covering all costs; extension fees will be negotiated.

result.title: PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS
result.summary: Proposals may be rejected as non-responsive if required information is missing; they should be concise, relevant, and explain technical terms in plain language. Include a signed cover letter on company letterhead with contact details for authorized representatives. Provide a project plan for the OPEB valuation covering methodology, GASB compliance, AVFPD data needs, milestones, completion/report schedule, and report contents: projected benefits, accrued liability, OPEB assets at market and actuarial values, unfunded liability, normal cost, required contribution in dollars and as payroll percentage, annual OPEB cost, net obligation, data and assumptions summaries, and GASB-format financial statement notes. Describe governmental and OPEB valuation experience; give municipal OPEB clients from the past 36 months and finance-officer contacts. Detail assigned staff experience and governmental-services training. Provide complete routine-service fees and hourly rates for additional services, a sample valuation, sample financial-statement notes and required supplementary information, and the latest financial statement with financial history/resources demonstrating stability. Disclose settlements and pending or past litigation from the last five years.

result.title: EVALUATION CRITERIA
result.summary:
EVALUATION CRITERIA
AVFPD will evaluate the responses and make a recommendation to the AVFPD Board for approval. The evaluation committee will consider the following factors:
1. Understanding of the services required.
2. Quality, clarity, and responsiveness of proposal.
3. Proposed fees.
6RFP for Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) Trust Actuarial Services
4. Information provided by client references.
5. Demonstrated competence and professional qualifications necessary for successfully performing the work required.
6. Background and related experience of the principal individuals to be assigned to provide services.
7. Approach in providing OPEB Trust actuarial consulting services.
8. Interviews, if conducted.

result.title: SELECTION PROCESS
result.summary:
SELECTION PROCESS
1. AVFPD will initially review all responses to determine responsiveness. Any response that does not address all requested requirements or is incomplete will be rejected.
2. AVFPD will evaluate all responses based on the criteria stated above. The evaluation committee may afford organizations the opportunity to clarify responses for the purpose of assuring a full understanding of their responsiveness to the RFP.
3. AVFPD may conduct interviews with firms found to be the most qualified to perform the services required, based upon the criteria listed in this RFP. If so, the firms will be notified in advance of the proposed interview date.
4. All responding firms will be notified in writing once one or more organizations have been selected and approved.

result.title: INSTRUCTIONS TO SUBMITTING FIRMS
result.summary: Submitting firms certify they have reviewed the RFP and can provide AVFPD quality, creative, cost-effective, service-oriented OPEB actuarial services. Questions must be emailed to Finance Officer Amber Exley by 4:00 p.m. July 29, 2024. Proposals must arrive by 11:59 p.m. PDT July 31, 2024, by email with the specified subject line or in a marked sealed envelope at the stated address; late proposals are rejected. Proposals may be withdrawn in writing before the deadline. AVFPD is not obligated to award a contract or reimburse proposal costs and reserves broad discretion over selection, rejection, timing, process corrections, subcontractors, negotiations, final offers, acceptance, and waiver of irregularities. Responses need a cover letter with office mailing address and primary contact details; they must be signed and irrevocable for 180 days. The successful firm must allow audits during the contract and for seven years afterward; AVFPD may terminate, postpone, or delay the contract by written notice. Contract talks begin after Board approval and may move to the next-ranked proposer if negotiations fail. Proposals must be genuine and noncollusive.
